title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄序
國家公天下為心誕敷文教建
學育才每三歲一大比以賓
興其賢能無非欲網羅海内
之士以代天工以乂天民以
蔦棐億萬年太平之盛乃天
順壬午秋復當論秀之期先
===
是山西藩臬重臣走幣聘儒
碩司文衡屆期合郡邑士子
川會而雲集者設棘而三試
之于時綱維其事則巡撫右
僉都御史韓雍防範於外則
監察御史茂彪叶恭贊襄則
左布政使張茂按察使王允
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄序
國家公天下為心，誕敷文教，建學育才。每三歲一大比，以賓興其賢能，無非欲網羅海内之士，以代天工，以乂天民，以蔦棐億萬年太平之盛。乃天順壬午秋，復當論秀之期。先是，山西藩臬重臣走幣聘儒碩司文衡。屆期，合郡邑士子川會而雲集者，設棘而三試之。于時綱維其事，則巡撫右僉都御史韓雍；防範於外，則監察御史茂彪；叶恭贊襄，則左布政使張茂、按察使王允、
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

Taking impartiality toward all under Heaven as its guiding heart, the dynasty broadly spreads civil teachings, establishing schools and nurturing talent. Every three years, a grand competition is held to recommend and elevate the worthy and capable as honored guests. This is solely out of a desire to gather the scholars within the seas to perform the work of Heaven on its behalf, to govern Heaven's people, and to support and assist [?] the flourishing of a billion myriad years of Great Peace. Now, in the autumn of the renwu year of the Tianshun era (1462), it was once again the time for evaluating and selecting the finest talents. Prior to this, the senior officials of the Shanxi Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions sent gifts to invite erudite Confucian scholars to take charge of the literary evaluations. When the appointed time arrived, the scholars from all the prefectures and districts who converged like rivers and gathered like clouds were placed inside the thorny enclosure and examined in three sessions. At that time, directing the affair as a whole was Grand Coordinator and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Han Yong 韓雍; maintaining security on the outside was Investigating Censor Mao Biao 茂彪; and cooperating respectfully to assist in the undertaking were Left Administration Commissioner Zhang Mao 張茂, Surveillance Commissioner Wang Yun 王允, …

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
左叅政魏琳右叅政劉福祝
顥副使張瑄滕佐左叅議楊
學右叅議徐行孫昱僉事強
宏朱瑄呂正錢俊鄭貞內而
監臨則廵按監察御史韓祺
提調則右布政使謝佑監試
則僉事倪通咸秉至公圖惟
===
得人撤棘取其文之中程度
者六十五人且次第其名氏
與其文之純者鋟梓以爲小
錄僉謂晃濫竽校文之末宜
序首簡以紀榮遇之盛竊惟
設科之制而取士以文非盡
德行也良以文章天下公器
punctuated: 左叅政魏琳、右叅政劉福、祝顥、副使張瑄、滕佐、左叅議楊學、右叅議徐行、孫昱、僉事強宏、朱瑄、呂正、錢俊、鄭貞，內而監臨則廵按監察御史韓祺，提調則右布政使謝佑，監試則僉事倪通，咸秉至公，圖惟得人。撤棘，取其文之中程度者六十五人，且次第其名氏與其文之純者，鋟梓以爲小錄。僉謂晃濫竽校文之末，宜序首簡，以紀榮遇之盛。竊惟設科之制，而取士以文，非盡德行也；良以文章天下公器，
translation_en: …Left Administration Vice Commissioner Wei Lin 魏琳, Right Administration Vice Commissioners Liu Fu 劉福 and Zhu Hao 祝顥, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhang Xuan 張瑄 and Teng Zuo 滕佐, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Yang Xue 楊學, Right Assistant Administration Commissioners Xu Xing 徐行 and Sun Yu 孫昱, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Qiang Hong 強宏, Zhu Xuan 朱瑄, Lü Zheng 呂正, Qian Jun 錢俊, and Zheng Zhen 鄭貞. Inside the examination compound, the Supervising Official was Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor Han Qi 韓祺, the Proctor was Right Administration Commissioner Xie You 謝佑, and the Examination Supervisor was Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Ni Tong 倪通. All of them upheld the utmost impartiality, seeking only to obtain worthy talent. When the thorny enclosure was removed, sixty-five men whose essays met the standard were selected, and their names were ranked in order along with the purest of their essays, which were carved onto printing blocks to make this small record. Everyone said that since I, [Pan] Huang 晃, unworthily occupied the lowest place among those evaluating the essays, I ought to write a preface for the opening pages to record the splendor of this glorious occasion. I privately reflect that in the institution of the civil service examinations, selecting scholars on the basis of their essays does not mean that moral conduct is wholly disregarded; rather, it is truly because literary composition is a public instrument of the realm,…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
而其言之所在德行攸寓仁
義道德之懿禮樂名物之盛
古今事變之迹皆於此焉考
見閱其文則兼德行而有之
矣故考校之際主司難其人
焉茍匪其人則文之紕駁士
之去取不直不明且不公必
===
無以收人望而得才實副設
科取士之盛意也翊山西古
冀州域士生其間服仁義而
佩詩書者自昔爲盛玆又遭
逢
盛世樂育庠序使通經學古皆
得以預賓興之會宜其掉鞅
punctuated: 而其言之所在，德行攸寓。仁義道德之懿，禮樂名物之盛，古今事變之迹，皆於此焉考見。閱其文，則兼德行而有之矣。故考校之際，主司難其人焉。茍匪其人，則文之紕駁，士之去取，不直、不明且不公，必無以收人望而得才實，副設科取士之盛意也。矧山西古冀州域，士生其間，服仁義而佩詩書者，自昔爲盛。玆又遭逢盛世，樂育庠序，使通經學古皆得以預賓興之會，宜其掉鞅
translation_en:
…and where one's words reside, there too one's virtuous conduct is lodged. The excellence of benevolence, righteousness, the Way, and virtue; the flourishing of rites, music, titles, and artifacts; and the traces of shifting affairs from antiquity to the present—all are examined and made visible therein. By reviewing their essays, one obtains their virtuous conduct alongside their writing. Therefore, at the time of examination and evaluation, it is difficult to find the right persons to serve as chief examiners. If they are not the right persons, then the flaws and impurities in the essays and the selection and rejection of the scholars will fail to be upright, discerning, and impartial; thus there will surely be no way to win popular confidence, obtain true talent, and fulfill the grand intent of establishing the examination categories to select scholars.

Moreover, Shanxi is the territory of ancient Jizhou; the scholars born within it who clothe themselves in benevolence and righteousness and wear the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu) at their girdles have been numerous since antiquity. Now they have also encountered a flourishing age that delights in nurturing them in the local schools, enabling all who master the Classics and study antiquity to participate in the gathering for the triennial recommendation of worthy talents. Fittingly, as theyvie for mastery in…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
文場褎然舉首以爲當時所
用而事竣得士止若干人遵
定制也然則登名是錄者其亦
榮幸矣哉行將角藝春闈對
揚
大廷駸駸乎顯融之地尚當以
所述之文闡猷凝績光輔太
平之治俾天下後世指而羨
===
曰
國家以公天下爲心而科目得
人之盛飛英聲騰茂實度越
前古比跡唐虞三代如此亦
職有利哉若大弄筆墨以徼
利祿是濟己私而負設科取
punctuated: 文場，褎然舉首，以爲當時所用。而事竣得士止若干人，遵定制也。然則登名是錄者，其亦榮幸矣哉！行將角藝春闈，對揚大廷，駸駸乎顯融之地，尚當以所述之文，闡猷凝績，光輔太平之治，俾天下後世指而羨曰：「國家以公天下爲心，而科目得人之盛，飛英聲、騰茂實，度越前古，比跡唐、虞、三代如此。」亦職有利哉！若大弄筆墨以徼利祿，是濟己私而負設科取
translation_en: … the examination arena, standing out at the head of the list to be employed by the present age. Yet when the affair was concluded, the scholars obtained numbered only so many, in compliance with the established quota. That being so, how glorious and fortunate indeed are those whose names are entered in this record! Soon they will compete in literary skill at the spring Metropolitan Examination, respond to the Sovereign in the Great Court, and advance rapidly toward illustrious and distinguished positions. They ought then to put into practice what they have expounded in their essays—unfolding grand counsels and consolidating achievements to gloriously assist the governance of Supreme Peace—so that the empire and posterity will point to them in admiration and say: "The Dynasty takes impartiality toward all under Heaven as its mind, and the flourishing of talent obtained through the examination system—spreading brilliant renown and raising rich substance—surpasses earlier antiquity and matches the footsteps of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties like this!" Would that not indeed be beneficial to the fulfillment of their offices? As for those who merely [? 大 for 夫] toy with brush and ink to seek profit and emolument, they are serving their own selfish interests and betraying the…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
士之
盛典矣惡逃天下後世之公論
哉庸書此以為諸士子勸云
浙江衢州府常山縣儒學教
諭唐冕序
punctuated:
士之盛典矣，惡逃天下後世之公論哉？庸書此以為諸士子勸云。
浙江衢州府常山縣儒學教諭唐冕序。
translation_en:
… the grand institution of [establishing examination categories to select] scholars! How could they escape the impartial judgment of the empire and of future generations? I therefore write this as an exhortation to all the scholars.
Preface by Tang Mian 唐冕, Instructor in the Confucian School of Changshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

text:

仰惟

太宗文皇帝御製爲善陰隲孝順事實二書
宣宗章皇帝御製五倫書其垂世立教之心與
六經四書心學相爲表裏者也然
大誥三書亦自相爲表裏歟孝順事實所載
有違孝巨孝孝忠忠孝孝與夫感鬼神格
鳥獸孚草木之孝爲善陰隲所載有仁
恕仁惠仁恤仁直與夫施財仁民愛物
之仁其名義事實可悉數而詳言之歟
抑亦與
大誥五倫書六經四書所載相通否歟諸士
子佩
===
綸音而誦聖訓有年于茲矣請著於篇
問六經皆孔子刪脩贊定者也然其間猶
不能盡信焉易有連山歸藏今止存周
易實更伏羲文王周公孔子四聖而成
punctuated:
問：聖人之心見於書，猶化工之妙著於物。仰惟太祖高皇帝御製《大誥》三編，太宗文皇帝御製《爲善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書，宣宗章皇帝御製《五倫書》，其垂世立教之心，與六經、四書心學相爲表裏者也。然《大誥》三書亦自相爲表裏歟？《孝順事實》所載，有違孝、巨孝、孝忠、忠孝孝，與夫感鬼神、格鳥獸、孚草木之孝；《爲善陰隲》所載，有仁恕、仁惠、仁恤、仁直，與夫施財、仁民、愛物之仁，其名義、事實可悉數而詳言之歟？抑亦與《大誥》、《五倫書》、六經、四書所載相通否歟？諸士子佩綸音而誦聖訓，有年于茲矣，請著於篇。

問：六經皆孔子刪脩贊定者也，然其間猶不能盡信焉。《易》有《連山》、《歸藏》，今止存《周易》，實更伏羲、文王、周公、孔子四聖而成，
translation_en:
Question: The mind of the sage is manifested in books just as the marvelous workings of nature are revealed in things. Looking up in reverence, we reflect that Emperor Taizu Gao composed the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao), Emperor Taizong Wen composed the two books Hidden Merits of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Accounts of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi), and Emperor Xuanzong Zhang composed the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu). Their intention in handing down teachings for posterity complements the learning of the mind-and-heart found in the Six Classics and the Four Books as outer and inner aspects of a whole. Yet do the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements also complement one another as outer and inner aspects? What is recorded in the True Accounts of Filial Piety includes filial piety that goes against convention [? 違孝], great filial piety, filial piety and loyalty, loyalty and filial piety [? 忠孝孝], as well as filial piety that moves ghosts and spirits, reaches birds and beasts, and inspires trust even in grasses and trees. What is recorded in the Hidden Merits of Doing Good includes benevolence and reciprocity, benevolence and kindness, benevolence and compassion, benevolence and uprightness, as well as the benevolence of bestowing wealth, being benevolent to the people, and loving creatures. Can their definitions and historical facts be fully enumerated and explained in detail? Or do they also interconnect with what is recorded in the Grand Pronouncements, the Book of the Five Human Relationships, the Six Classics, and the Four Books, or not? You scholars have cherished the imperial words and recited the sage instructions for years now; please set forth your answers in your essays.

Question: The Six Classics were all expurgated, edited, praised, and settled by Confucius, yet among accounts of them there are still things that cannot be entirely believed. Of the Changes (Yi), there were the Lianshan and the Guizang, while today only the Changes of Zhou (Zhouyi) survives; in truth it was completed by passing through the hands of four sages—Fuxi, King Wen, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius—…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
說者謂入吏三聖何歟書之堯典紀唐
堯之事何以謂虞書禹貢紀於唐虞之
際何以謂夏書詩之王風宜為雅而為
風魯頌宜為風而為頌春秋以周正紀
事而冠以夏時經成麟應乃以為感麟
而作何歟禮樂所載吉凶賓嘉皆有禮
而軍禮獨缺自天子至士皆有冠禮而
大夫獨缺樂以象成變之制而為賞諸
侯舞必有坐致右憲左而曰非武坐又
何歟此皆有疑於心而未解者也願相
與折衷之
===
問元首明而股肱良此自然之理也唐虞
三代明良相逢固無容議後世言治者
必曰漢唐宋當時賢相漢稱蕭曹丙魏
唐稱房杜姚宋宋稱韓范富歐其功業
可得而言歟他如汲黯韓愈程顥張載
使之亦居相位其功業聞望視前數君
子果軒輊歟諸葛孔明晉之卞壼皆表
punctuated:
說者謂入吏三聖，何歟？《書》之〈堯典〉紀唐堯之事，何以謂〈虞書〉？〈禹貢〉紀於唐、虞之際，何以謂〈夏書〉？《詩》之〈王風〉宜為〈雅〉而為〈風〉，〈魯頌〉宜為〈風〉而為〈頌〉；《春秋》以周正紀事而冠以夏時，經成麟應，乃以為感麟而作，何歟？禮樂所載，吉、凶、賓、嘉皆有禮，而軍禮獨缺；自天子至士皆有冠禮，而大夫獨缺；樂以象成，變之制而為賞諸侯；舞必有坐，致右憲左，而曰「非武坐」，又何歟？此皆有疑於心而未解者也，願相與折衷之。
問：元首明而股肱良，此自然之理也。唐、虞、三代，明良相逢，固無容議。後世言治者，必曰漢、唐、宋。當時賢相，漢稱蕭、曹、丙、魏，唐稱房、杜、姚、宋，宋稱韓、范、富、歐，其功業可得而言歟？他如汲黯、韓愈、程顥、張載，使之亦居相位，其功業聞望視前數君子，果軒輊歟？諸葛孔明、晉之卞壼，皆表
translation_en:
…yet commentators say that "humans passed through [?] three sages"—why is that? In the Book of Documents (Shu), the "Canon of Yao" ("Yaodian") records the affairs of Yao of Tang, so why is it called a Book of Yu ("Yushu")? The "Tribute of Yu" ("Yugong") was recorded during the transition between Tang and Yu, so why is it called a Book of Xia ("Xiashu")? In the Book of Odes (Shi), the "Airs of the Royal Domain" ("Wangfeng") ought to be among the "Odes" ("Ya") yet are classed as "Airs" ("Feng"), and the "Hymns of Lu" ("Lusong") ought to be "Airs" yet are classed as "Hymns" ("Song"); the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records events using the Zhou calendar yet heads them with the Xia seasons, and though the unicorn responded when the Classic was completed, it is instead considered to have been composed out of emotion at seeing the unicorn—why is that? In what is recorded of ritual and music, auspicious, inauspicious, guest, and felicitous occasions all have their rites, yet the military rites alone are lacking; from the Son of Heaven down to the serviceman (shi), all have capping rites, yet the grand masters (daifu) alone lack them; music is meant to symbolize accomplishment, yet the institution of Kui [?] was turned into a reward for the feudal lords; in dance there is necessarily kneeling, bringing the right knee to the ground while raising the left, yet it is said, "This is not the kneeling of Martial Music (Wu)"—why, again, is this? These are all matters about which I harbor doubts in my mind and which remain unresolved; I wish to weigh and judge them together with you.

Question: When the sovereign is enlightened, his ministers are upright—this is a natural principle. In the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, enlightened rulers and upright ministers met with one another; of this there is certainly no need for discussion. Those in later ages who speak of good governance invariably cite the Han, Tang, and Song. As for the worthy Chief Councilors of those times, in the Han one praises Xiao [Xiao He 蕭何], Cao [Cao Can 曹參], Bing [Bing Ji 丙吉], and Wei [Wei Xiang 魏相]; in the Tang one praises Fang [Fang Xuanling 房玄齡], Du [Du Ruhui 杜如晦], Yao [Yao Chong 姚崇], and Song [Song Jing 宋璟]; and in the Song one praises Han [Han Qi 韓琦], Fan [Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹], Fu [Fu Bi 富弼], and Ou [Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩]. Can their achievements and enterprises be recounted? As for others such as Ji An 汲黯, Han Yu 韓愈, Cheng Hao 程顥, and Zhang Zai 張載, had they also occupied the position of Chief Councilor, how would their achievements, enterprises, and renown have compared in weight with those of the several gentlemen mentioned before? Zhuge Kongming 諸葛孔明 [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮] and Bian Kun 卞壼 of the Jin were both…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
表可稱者也乃不能復漢祚而興晉業
其故何歟使其得事漢唐宋盛時之君
界無愧於前數君子之功業聞望否歟
諸生明體適用尚友千古其於昔人之
相業景仰素矣行將見用以縻好爵果
取法於何人歟抑亦別有所願歟請明
言以對
問學校所以作養人才以待用科目所以
簡拔賢才以見用稽諸古而有教授蘇
===
湖而人才明體用之學者有持衡宋室
而人才數正直之對者可指其人而實
其事歟洪惟
聖朝建學育才設科取士良法美意至矣盡矣
邇者尚屢
宸衷命憲臣以督學政定解額以嚴選舉其故
何歟茲欲不待憲臣之督而學校得人
如古人教授蘇湖人才得明體用之學
其責奚歸不待解額之限而科目得人
punctuated:
表可稱者也，乃不能復漢祚而興晉業，其故何歟？使其得事漢、唐、宋盛時之君，界無愧於前數君子之功業聞望否歟？諸生明體適用，尚友千古，其於昔人之相業，景仰素矣。行將見用以縻好爵，果取法於何人歟？抑亦別有所願歟？請明言以對。

問：學校所以作養人才以待用，科目所以簡拔賢才以見用。稽諸古，而有教授蘇湖，而人才明體用之學者；有持衡宋室，而人才數正直之對者。可指其人而實其事歟？洪惟聖朝，建學育才，設科取士，良法美意，至矣盡矣。邇者尚屢宸衷，命憲臣以督學政，定解額以嚴選舉，其故何歟？茲欲不待憲臣之督，而學校得人，如古人教授蘇湖，人才得明體用之學，其責奚歸？不待解額之限，而科目得人，
translation_en:
…outstanding and praiseworthy, yet they were unable to restore the fortune of the Han or revive the enterprise of the Jin—what is the reason for this? Had they been able to serve the rulers of the flourishing ages of the Han, Tang, or Song, would they generally [?] have had no cause for shame beside the achievements and renown of those several gentlemen mentioned earlier, or not? You students understand both fundamental principles and practical application, and you befriend the ancients across a thousand ages; you have long admired the ministerial achievements of the men of the past. Soon you will be employed and bound by fine office—whom, indeed, will you take as your model? Or do you have some other aspiration? Please state your reply clearly.

Question: Schools are the means by which men of talent are nurtured and cultivated to await employment; examination categories are the means by which worthy talents are selected and promoted to be put to use. Examining antiquity, there was one who taught in Suzhou and Huzhou, so that men of talent understood the learning of substance and function; and there was one who held the balance of the examinations under the Song house, so that men of talent were noted for their upright replies. Can you point out who these men were and substantiate their deeds? Greatly reflecting upon Our Sacred Dynasty, which has established schools to nurture talent and instituted examination categories to select scholars, its fine laws and admirable intentions have reached the utmost perfection. Yet recently this has still repeatedly occupied the imperial mind, so that censorial officials have been commanded to supervise education administration and quotas of provincial graduates have been fixed to make selection strict—what is the reason for this? Now, if we wish that without waiting for the supervision of censorial officials, the schools should obtain the right men—just as when that ancient taught in Suzhou and Huzhou, and men of talent acquired the learning of substance and function—where does that responsibility lie? And if we wish that without waiting for the restriction of graduate quotas, the examination categories should obtain the right men…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
如古人持衡宋室賢材得數正直之對
其術安在諸生會際賓興進退係之願
著于篇毋讓
問知者無不知也當務之爲急山右地連
朔漠今之先務備邊儲運安民息訟四
者爲急
聖朝嘗選將練兵矣而醜虜尚為邊患嘗輸粟
實邊矣而士卒尚慮不給茲欲内脩外
攘軍民安輯邊儲充裕將士賈勇如古
===
人圖上方略坐困西羌撓漕調兵未嘗
乏絕其道何繇嘗布德宣惠矣而斯民
未免轉徙於他境嘗命官折獄矣而奸
頑未免日流於健訟茲欲來流移而安
土著鋤強梗而扶善良如古人編户增
至八萬餘口閉閤思過而百姓感化其
法安在諸士子生長茲土於數者飫聞
而厭見矣幸明言之以觀用世之學
punctuated:
如古人持衡宋室，賢材得數正直之對，其術安在？諸生會際賓興，進退係之，願著于篇，毋讓。

問：「知者無不知也，當務之爲急。」山右地連朔漠，今之先務，備邊、儲運、安民、息訟四者爲急。聖朝嘗選將練兵矣，而醜虜尚為邊患；嘗輸粟實邊矣，而士卒尚慮不給。茲欲内脩外攘，軍民安輯，邊儲充裕，將士賈勇，如古人圖上方略，坐困西羌，撓漕調兵，未嘗乏絕，其道何繇？嘗布德宣惠矣，而斯民未免轉徙於他境；嘗命官折獄矣，而奸頑未免日流於健訟。茲欲來流移而安土著，鋤強梗而扶善良，如古人編户增至八萬餘口，閉閤思過而百姓感化，其法安在？諸士子生長茲土，於數者飫聞而厭見矣，幸明言之，以觀用世之學。
translation_en:
…like the ancients who held the balance of recruitment for the Song house and obtained worthy talents who repeatedly offered upright responses—where does the method for this lie? You students now meet with this grand occasion of the triennial examination, upon which your advancement or withdrawal depends. We hope you will set forth your views in your essays without holding back.

Question: "The wise know everything, but they regard what is urgently needed as their priority." Shanxi's territory borders the northern deserts; among today's primary tasks, the four matters of frontier defense, grain storage and transport, pacifying the people, and curbing litigation are the most urgent. Our Sacred Dynasty has already selected generals and trained troops, yet the vile caitiffs still pose a threat on the frontier; it has already transported grain to stock the borders, yet there is still concern that the soldiers are insufficiently supplied. Now, if we wish to cultivate governance internally and repel threats externally, so that soldiers and civilians are at peace, frontier provisions are abundant, and officers and men muster their courage—just like the ancients who submitted illustrated strategic plans to effortlesslyhem in the Western Qiang, or who amid disrupted grain transport and troop deployments never suffered a shortage of supplies—by what way can this be achieved? We have already spread virtue and proclaimed benevolence, yet the people still cannot avoid wandering away to other regions; we have already appointed officials to adjudicate legal cases, yet thecrafty and obstinate still cannot avoid sinking daily into litigiousness. Now, if we wish to attract wandering migrants back and settle the native inhabitants, and weed out the violent and obstructive while supporting the good and law-abiding—just like the ancients under whom registered households increased by over eighty thousand mouths, or who shut themselves in their chambers to reflect on their faults so that the common people were moved and transformed—where does the method for this lie? You gentlemen were born and raised in this land, and have heard and seen your fill of these several matters. Please state your views clearly, so that we may observe your learning for practical service to the world.

四書
禮云禮云玉帛云乎哉樂云樂云鍾鼓云
乎哉
王璜

聖人論禮樂所以爲禮樂不專事其末焉蓋禮
===
樂有本而有末也遺其本而專事其末則豈禮
樂之謂哉思昔吾夫子言此以矯當時之弊其
意謂夫敬而將之以玉帛則爲禮禮也者敬爲
之本而玉帛其末耳特世之爲禮者知玉帛之
交錯而不知禮之本在於敬若言禮之全體必
本末兼盡而後可苟徒玉帛之是尚而不以敬
爲之主則是棄本逐末矣烏得謂之禮乎和而
發之以鍾鼓則爲樂樂也者和爲之本而鍾鼓
其末耳特世之爲樂者知鍾鼓之鏗鏘而不知
punctuated:
四書

「禮云禮云，玉帛云乎哉？樂云樂云，鍾鼓云乎哉？」

聖人論禮樂所以爲禮樂，不專事其末焉。蓋禮樂有本而有末也，遺其本而專事其末，則豈禮樂之謂哉？思昔吾夫子言此以矯當時之弊，其意謂：夫敬而將之以玉帛，則爲禮。禮也者，敬爲之本，而玉帛其末耳。特世之爲禮者，知玉帛之交錯，而不知禮之本在於敬。若言禮之全體，必本末兼盡而後可。苟徒玉帛之是尚，而不以敬爲之主，則是棄本逐末矣，烏得謂之禮乎？和而發之以鍾鼓，則爲樂。樂也者，和爲之本，而鍾鼓其末耳。特世之爲樂者，知鍾鼓之鏗鏘，而不知
translation_en:
The Four Books

"'Ritual, they say, ritual!' Does it mean no more than jade and silk? 'Music, they say, music!' Does it mean no more than bells and drums?" [Analects 17.11]

Wang Huang 王璜

Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Luo comments: The topic is inherently difficult to phrase well, yet the reasoning and style of this essay are concise and clear; it truly deserves to be selected for publication.
Examiner Instructor Dai comments: It deeply accords with the fundamental purport of the passage, and therefore we single it out for publication.
Examiner Instructor Tang comments: This composition is neither vague nor cursory; it is worthy of selection.

When the Sage discussed that by which ritual and music constitute ritual and music, he showed that they do not consist solely in attending to their secondary manifestations. For ritual and music have both their fundamentals and their secondary manifestations; if one neglects their fundamentals and attends solely to their secondary manifestations, how can that be called ritual and music? Reflecting on the past, when our Master spoke these words to rectify the abuses of his time, his meaning was this: When reverence is conveyed through jade and silk, it constitutes ritual. In ritual, reverence is the fundamental, whereas jade and silk are merely its secondary manifestations. It is only that those in the world who practice ritual know thecrisscrossing exchange of jade and silk, yet do not know that the fundamental of ritual lies in reverence. If one speaks of ritual in its entirety, only when both the fundamental and the secondary are fully realized can it be deemed proper. If one merely prizes jade and silk without making reverence the master, then that is abandoning the fundamental to pursue the secondary—how could it be called ritual? When harmony is expressed through bells and drums, it constitutes music. In music, harmony is the fundamental, whereas bells and drums are merely its secondary manifestations. It is only that those in the world who perform music know the ringing resonance of bells and drums, yet do not know…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
樂之本在於和若言樂之全體必本末具舉而
後可苟惟鍾鼓之是尚而不以和爲之主則是
徇末忘本矣烏得謂之樂乎大抵玉帛可以行
禮也謂玉帛爲非禮則不可鍾鼓可以爲樂也
謂鍾鼓爲非樂亦不可然禮樂豈止玉帛鍾鼓
之間哉得其本則玉帛鍾鼓莫非情文之所寓
不然是虛器而已聖人因當時文勝滅質故特
言此以矯其弊厥有旨哉
誠者自成也而道自道也誠者物之終始
不誠無物是故君子誠之爲貴誠者非自
成己而已也所以成物也成己仁也成物
知也性之德也合內外之道也故時措之
宜也
趙傅

樂之本在於和。若言樂之全體，必本末具舉而後可。苟惟鍾鼓之是尚，而不以和爲之主，則是徇末忘本矣，烏得謂之樂乎？大抵玉帛可以行禮也，謂玉帛爲非禮則不可；鍾鼓可以爲樂也，謂鍾鼓爲非樂亦不可。然禮樂豈止玉帛鍾鼓之間哉？得其本，則玉帛鍾鼓莫非情文之所寓；不然，是虛器而已。聖人因當時文勝滅質，故特言此以矯其弊，厥有旨哉！

「誠者自成也，而道自道也。誠者物之終始，不誠無物。是故君子誠之爲貴。誠者非自成己而已也，所以成物也。成己，仁也；成物，知也。性之德也，合內外之道也，故時措之宜也。」
趙傅

translation_en:
… the foundation of music lies in harmony. If one speaks of music in its entirety, only when both the fundamental and the incidental are upheld together will it suffice. If one merely prizes bells and drums without making harmony their governing principle, then one is pursuing the incidental and forgetting the fundamental—how could that be called music? Generally speaking, jade and silk can be used to perform ritual, so it is wrong to say that jade and silk are not ritual; bells and drums can be used to make music, so it is likewise wrong to say that bells and drums are not music. Yet how could ritual and music be confined merely to jade and silk or bells and drums? When their foundation is attained, jade, silk, bells, and drums are all where genuine feeling and refined form reside; otherwise, they are nothing more than empty vessels. Because in his time outward refinement had overwhelmed and extinguished substantial reality, the Sage specially spoke these words to rectify that failing—how profound was his meaning!

"Sincerity is self-completion, and the Way is self-directed. Sincerity is the beginning and end of things; without sincerity there would be nothing. Therefore the noble man values attaining sincerity. Sincerity is not merely completing oneself; it is that whereby one completes all things. Completing oneself is humanity (ren); completing things is wisdom (zhi). These are the virtues of one's nature, and the Way that unites the inner and the outer; therefore, whenever it is applied, it is fitting." [Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), ch. 25]
By Zhao Fu 趙傅.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Jiang 蔣: [Most of those writing on this topic do not know that "sincerity" refers to both principle (li) and the mind (xin). This essay succeeds in elucidating this and truly deserves a high recommendation.]
Comment by Examiner Instructor Dai 戴: [The diction suffices to convey the meaning; it is commendable.]
Comment by Examiner Instructor Tang 唐: [The explanation of principle is detailed and clear, amply demonstrating his learning and insight.]

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
誠寓人物而無遺在人當實其心誠貫體用而
無間處事斯得其當蓋誠之在物在人雖有實
理實心之殊而成己成物實無仁知內外之間
則其見之於事又豈不得時措之宜也哉且實
理之在物謂之誠是誠也天地人物之類所以
自成而不假於人為焉實心之在人謂之道是
道也君臣父子之屬所當自行而非有待於外
焉惟其誠者自成也是以天下之物皆實理之
所為故必得是理然後有是物所得之理既盡
===
則是物亦盡而無有矣惟其而道自道也是以
在人之心一有不實則雖有所為亦如無有而
君子必實其心而以誠為貴焉誠雖所以成己
然既有以自成則自然及物而道之在我者亦
行於彼故成不自成而必有以成乎物焉自成
己言之克己復禮無少私偽故謂之仁自成物
言之因物成就各得其當故謂之知仁者體之
存知者用之發是皆吾性之固有而無內外之
殊既得於己則其見於事者以時措之而皆得
punctuated: 誠寓人物而無遺，在人當實其心；誠貫體用而無間，處事斯得其當。蓋誠之在物在人，雖有實理實心之殊，而成己成物，實無仁知內外之間，則其見之於事，又豈不得時措之宜也哉？且實理之在物謂之誠，是誠也，天地人物之類所以自成而不假於人為焉；實心之在人謂之道，是道也，君臣父子之屬所當自行而非有待於外焉。惟其誠者自成也，是以天下之物，皆實理之所為，故必得是理，然後有是物，所得之理既盡，則是物亦盡而無有矣。惟其而道自道也，是以在人之心，一有不實，則雖有所為，亦如無有，而君子必實其心而以誠為貴焉。誠雖所以成己，然既有以自成，則自然及物，而道之在我者，亦行於彼，故成不自成，而必有以成乎物焉。自成己言之，克己復禮，無少私偽，故謂之仁；自成物言之，因物成就，各得其當，故謂之知。仁者體之存，知者用之發，是皆吾性之固有，而無內外之殊。既得於己，則其見於事者，以時措之而皆得
translation_en:
Sincerity resides in humans and things without omission, so in a person one ought to make one's mind real; sincerity penetrates substance and function without gap, so in handling affairs one thereby attains what is proper. For although sincerity as it exists in things and in humans has the distinction between real principle and a real mind, in completing oneself and completing things there is truly no gap between benevolence and wisdom, or inner and outer; when it is manifested in affairs, how then could it fail to attain the appropriateness of timely application?

Moreover, real principle as it exists in things is called sincerity. This sincerity is that whereby such categories as Heaven, Earth, humans, and things complete themselves without borrowing from human artifice. A real mind as it exists in humans is called the Way. This Way is that which those in relations such as ruler and minister, father and son ought to practice of themselves without depending on anything external. Because "sincerity is self-completion," all things in the world are made by real principle; therefore, only after obtaining this principle does a thing exist, and once the principle it has obtained is exhausted, that thing too is exhausted and ceases to exist. And because "the Way is self-directed," if in a person's mind there is a single instance of unreality, then even though one does something, it is as if nothing were done; thus the noble man must make his mind real and hold sincerity to be precious.

Although sincerity is the means of completing oneself, once one has the means to complete oneself, it naturally extends to things, and the Way that is within me is also practiced toward them; therefore completion is not merely completing oneself, but must also be the means of completing things. Spoken of in terms of completing oneself, overcoming the self and returning to propriety without the slightest selfish falsity is therefore called benevolence; spoken of in terms of completing things, following things to bring them to completion so that each attains what is proper to it is therefore called wisdom. Benevolence is the preservation of substance, and wisdom is the issuance of function; these are both inherent in our nature, without distinction between inner and outer. Once this is attained in oneself, then in its manifestation in affairs, one applies it according to the time and in all cases attains…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
其宜以義處之而各當其可矣所以然者何莫
而非一誠之所爲哉抑考中庸是章以誠之者
之知發明人道所謂自明而誠者也章内之言
雖散而不一要而言之一誠而已矣大哉誠乎
其所以爲造化之樞紐品彙之根柢兼理與心
而言者乎
今曰性善然則彼皆非與孟子曰乃若其
情則可以爲善矣乃所謂善也
陳壁
===
同考試官訓導王　批〔諸作於彼皆非與處大體總分明此篇得之令人注目〕

門人舉夫性善而疑衆說之非大賢告以因情
而知所性之善夫情者性之動情善則性善矣
大賢因門人舉性善而質其疑安得不以此而
告之哉思昔公都子問於孟子之意若曰天下
之言性者多矣今而夫子獨曰性善而無惡則
punctuated:
其宜，以義處之而各當其可矣。所以然者，何莫而非一誠之所爲哉！抑考《中庸》是章，以誠之者之知發明人道，所謂「自明而誠」者也。章内之言雖散而不一，要而言之，一誠而已矣。大哉誠乎！其所以爲造化之樞紐、品彙之根柢，兼理與心而言者乎！

「今曰『性善』，然則彼皆非與？」孟子曰：「乃若其情，則可以爲善矣，乃所謂善也。」
陳壁

門人舉夫性善而疑衆說之非，大賢告以因情而知所性之善。夫情者，性之動；情善則性善矣。大賢因門人舉性善而質其疑，安得不以此而告之哉！思昔公都子問於孟子之意，若曰：天下之言性者多矣，今而夫子獨曰性善而無惡，則
translation_en:
… what is appropriate, and when handled with righteousness, each accords with what is proper. Why this is so—how could any of it not be the work of a single sincerity! Moreover, if we examine this chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), it uses the knowledge of one who attains sincerity to elucidate the way of humanity, which is what is meant by "proceeding from enlightenment to sincerity." Although the words within the chapter are dispersed and varied, in sum, they amount to nothing more than a single sincerity. Great indeed is sincerity! Is it not that which serves as the pivot of creation and transformation, the foundation of all things, and is spoken of as encompassing both principle and the mind!

"Now you say, 'Human nature is good.' Then are all those others wrong?" Mencius (Mengzi) said, "As for its genuine feelings, they are capable of being good. This is what I mean by being good."
Chen Bi 陳壁

Examiner and Instructor Dai 戴 comments: 〔Fluent and well worth reading.〕
Examiner and Instructor Tang 唐 comments: 〔Skillfully able to elucidate the meaning of the theme; one who is profound in fundamental mastery.〕

The disciple cited the doctrine that human nature is good and doubted whether the various other theories were wrong; the Great Worthy answered him by explaining how through the feelings one can know the goodness of the nature one is endowed with. Now, feelings are the movements of human nature; if the feelings are good, then the nature is good. Since the Great Worthy's disciple cited the goodness of human nature to resolve his doubts, how could he not tell him this! Reflecting on the past, the purport of Gongduzi's 公都子 question to Mencius was as if to say: Those in the world who speak of human nature are many. Now you, Master, alone say that human nature is good and without evil; then…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
告子所謂性無善無不善之旨似非至論賦天
下之論性者衆矣今而夫子乃曰性善無不善
則或人所謂性可以爲善可以爲不善有性善
有性不善之言皆非確論歟公都子之問若此
故孟子從而告之以謂性藴於中而難言情發
於外而易見如見孺子入井而惻隱之心生遇
嘑蹴之食而羞惡之心起此人之情本但可以
爲善而不可以爲惡也情之善也如此則仁義
之性本善可知矣過廟朝而恭敬之心形見羨
===
惡而是非之心著亦人之情本但可以爲善而
不可以爲惡也情之善也如此則禮知之性本
善可知矣是乃所以爲性善而公都子所疑之
三說庸何惑哉抑考孟子他章於告子問生之
謂性則折之性猶杞柳則責之性猶湍水則畧
加明辯至此公都子因論性善而質其疑則究
而告之以是何耶盖告子不求諸心故其言畧
公都子篤信孟子故其言詳此又不可不知
易
punctuated:
告子所謂「性無善無不善」之旨，似非至論賦？天下之論性者衆矣，今而夫子乃曰性善無不善，則或人所謂「性可以爲善，可以爲不善」、「有性善，有性不善」之言，皆非確論歟？公都子之問若此。故孟子從而告之，以謂性藴於中而難言，情發於外而易見。如見孺子入井而惻隱之心生，遇嘑蹴之食而羞惡之心起，此人之情本但可以爲善，而不可以爲惡也。情之善也如此，則仁義之性本善可知矣。過廟朝而恭敬之心形，見羨惡而是非之心著，亦人之情本但可以爲善，而不可以爲惡也。情之善也如此，則禮知之性本善可知矣。是乃所以爲性善，而公都子所疑之三說，庸何惑哉？抑考《孟子》他章，於告子問「生之謂性」則折之，「性猶杞柳」則責之，「性猶湍水」則畧加明辯；至此公都子因論性善而質其疑，則究而告之以是，何耶？盖告子不求諸心，故其言畧；公都子篤信孟子，故其言詳。此又不可不知。
《易》
translation_en:
… is not Gaozi's (告子) thesis that "human nature is neither good nor bad" seemingly short of the ultimate discourse [? 賦 for 歟]? Those in the world who discuss human nature are numerous; now since you, Master, say that human nature is good and has nothing not good, then are the claims by some that "human nature may be made to practice good and may be made to practice what is not good" and that "the nature of some is good and the nature of others is not good" both not definitive theories? Gongduzi's (公都子) question was to this effect. Therefore Mencius (孟子) answered him accordingly, saying that human nature is stored within and is difficult to speak of, whereas the feelings issue forth on the outside and are easy to see. For instance, when one sees a child about to fall into a well, a heart of compassion arises; when one encounters food given with an insulting shout or a kick, a heart of shame and dislike arises—this shows that human feelings by their root are capable of doing what is good, and are not capable of doing evil. Since the goodness of the feelings is like this, one can know that the nature of benevolence and righteousness is originally good. When one passes an ancestral temple or the court, a heart of reverence and respect takes form; when one sees what is admirable or detestable [? 羨惡 for 美惡], a heart of approving and disapproving becomes manifest—this likewise shows that human feelings by their root are capable of doing what is good, and are not capable of doing evil. Since the goodness of the feelings is like this, one can know that the nature of propriety and wisdom is originally good. This is what is meant by human nature being good—so how could one be perplexed by the three theories about which Gongduzi was in doubt? Furthermore, if we examine other chapters of the Mencius, when Gaozi proposed that "what is inborn is what is called nature," Mencius refuted him; when he said that "human nature is like the curling willow," Mencius rebuked him; and when he said that "human nature is like whirling water," Mencius only briefly offered a clear rebuttal. Yet when we come to this passage, where Gongduzi raised his doubts on the basis of the doctrine that human nature is good, Mencius thoroughly explained it to him in these terms—why is this? It is because Gaozi did not seek it in the mind, and therefore Mencius's words to him were brief; whereas Gongduzi earnestly believed in Mencius, and therefore Mencius's words to him were detailed. This, too, one must not fail to know.

Book of Changes (Yi 易)

九二大車以載有攸往无咎

爻以剛中而上應故聖人擬其象而予其占也
夫大有之重任未易以勝之也自非九二剛中
上應足以任其重焉奚能有往而無過哉是宜
===
爻易聖人係其象占如此且夫大有之卦合離
乾而成體爻至九二以陽剛得中之才而上應
六五文明之主剛健而有為中立而不倚當大
有之時以大才而當大任故有大車以載之象
焉夫車大則勝重才大則勝任輪輻強壯足以
載乎物衡軛周正足以致乎遠負荷雖多也量
足以容之而不負其所託之專倚任雖隆也才
足以當之而能保其所有之大象既著矣占而
值此者以之有所往而如是其德不往則已往
punctuated:
「九二，大車以載，有攸往，无咎。」

爻以剛中而上應，故聖人擬其象而予其占也。夫大有之重任，未易以勝之也。自非九二剛中上應，足以任其重焉，奚能有往而無過哉？是宜爻《易》聖人係其象占如此。且夫大有之卦，合離、乾而成體。爻至九二，以陽剛得中之才，而上應六五文明之主，剛健而有為，中立而不倚。當大有之時，以大才而當大任，故有「大車以載」之象焉。夫車大則勝重，才大則勝任。輪輻強壯，足以載乎物；衡軛周正，足以致乎遠。負荷雖多也，量足以容之，而不負其所託之專；倚任雖隆也，才足以當之，而能保其所有之大。象既著矣，占而值此者，以之有所往而如是其德，不往則已，往
translation_en:
"Nine in the second place: A large wagon for loading. Undertakings bring no blame." [Book of Changes (Yijing), Hexagram 14, Dayou (Possession in Great Measure)]
Chen Bi 陳璧
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wang 王 comments: [The diction and reasoning are grounded in the Original Meaning (Benyi 本義). It brings out the import of the image and the prognostication so that they are clearly before the eyes; it is not comparable to those that indulge in superficial generalities, and deserves to head this examination ward.]
Examiner and Instructor Dai 戴 comments: [The reasoning is clear and the phrasing smooth; surely this is someone deeply versed in the study of the Changes.]
Examiner and Instructor Tang 唐 comments: [The words suffice to convey the meaning, and therefore we single it out for presentation.]

Because the line possesses firm centrality and responds to the ruler above, the sage likens it to an image and grants it a prognostication. Now, the heavy responsibilities of a time of Possession in Great Measure (Dayou) are not easily borne. Unless it were Nine in the Second Place, whose firm centrality and responsiveness to the ruler above suffice to shoulder that weight, how could one go forward and remain free of fault? Thus it is fitting that the sage who composed the line statements of the Changes attached its image and prognostication in this manner.

Moreover, the hexagram Dayou combines the trigrams Li 離 and Qian 乾 to form its structure. When the lines reach Nine in the Second Place, with the talent of yang firmness attaining the mean, it responds above to Six in the Fifth Place, the enlightened ruler—firm, vigorous, and capable of action, standing in the middle without leaning to either side. In the time of Possession in Great Measure, bringing great talent to bear upon a great responsibility, it therefore has the image of "a large wagon for loading." Now, when a wagon is large, it can bear heavy loads; when talent is great, it can bear heavy responsibilities. Its wheels and spokes are strong and sturdy, sufficient to carry things; its crossbar and yoke are square and true, sufficient to reach afar. Although the burdens carried are many, his capacity suffices to contain them without betraying the exclusive trust placed in him; although the reliance and responsibility are exalted, his talent suffices to match them and preserve the greatness of all that is possessed. Once the image is made manifest, for one who obtains this in divination and goes forward with such virtue: if he does not go forward, nothing more need be said; if he goes forward…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
則無曳輪之阻而可以補其過焉以之有所行
而如此其才不行則已行則無說輹之虞而可
以免其咎焉聖人係九二之爻著其象而定其
占至是寧復有餘蘊哉試嘗圖之伊尹之相商
也感三聘之勤受阿衡之寄嘗曰予弗克俾厥
后惟堯舜其心愧恥若撻於市一夫不獲則曰
時予之辜其自任以天下之重如此是即大車
以載之謂矣噫大有九二不歸諸斯人而誰歟
繼之者善也成之者性也仁者見之謂之
===
仁知者見之謂之知
杜誠

夫道無往而不在也見於流行賦予者固有其
序而仁知偏於所見又豈得道之全體哉今夫
punctuated:
則無曳輪之阻，而可以補其過焉。以之有所行，而如此其才，不行則已，行則無說輹之虞，而可以免其咎焉。聖人係九二之爻，著其象而定其占，至是寧復有餘蘊哉？試嘗圖之：伊尹之相商也，感三聘之勤，受阿衡之寄，嘗曰：「予弗克俾厥后惟堯舜，其心愧恥，若撻於市。」一夫不獲，則曰：「時予之辜。」其自任以天下之重如此，是即「大車以載」之謂矣。噫！大有九二，不歸諸斯人而誰歟？

「繼之者善也，成之者性也。仁者見之謂之仁，知者見之謂之知。」

translation_en:
…then there will be no hindrance of dragging the wheels, and one can make up for one's faults. If with this one undertakes an action, possessing such talent as this—should one not act, there is no more to be said; but if one acts, there will be no worry of the axle-straps coming undone, and one can avoid blame. When the Sage appended the text to the Second Nine line, setting forth its image and determining its divination, by this point could there remain any unexpressed meaning? Let us try to illustrate this: When Yi Yin 伊尹 served as chief minister of Shang, moved by the earnestness of three invitations, he accepted the charge of Aheng 阿衡. He once said: "If I cannot make my sovereign like Yao 堯 and Shun 舜, my heart feels ashamed, as if beaten in the marketplace." And if a single man failed to find his place, he would say: "It is my fault!" His taking upon himself the heavy burden of the world was like this; this is precisely what is meant by "a great wagon for loading." Alas! If the Second Nine of "Great Possession" (Dayou 大有) is not attributed to such a man, then to whom?

"That which ensues from it is goodness; that which is completed by it is nature. The humane see it and call it humaneness; the wise see it and call it wisdom."
Du Cheng 杜誠

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
道具於陰而行乎陽以其方出而未賦於物則
繼之者謂之善焉繼言其發而善則化育之功
觀夫往過來續流動充滿於槖籥之間舊禪新
繹絪緼交密於亭毒之表純而不雜善而無惡
是即萬物統體是道之時陽之事也及其已出
而賦於物則成之者謂之性焉成言其具而性
則物之所受觀夫保合太和而全其混融之氣
各正性命而固其陰陽之理不相假借不相凌
奪是即萬物各具是道之時陰之事也然道之
===
全體本無不具而人之氣禀或不能齊是以仁
者之人禀陽氣之多但見是道流動而無窮充
滿而無間遂目道之全體止於仁而不知仁之
外復有知焉知者之人禀陰氣之多惟見是道
貞靜而不擾收斂而不露竟謂道之全體止於
知而不知知之外復有仁焉噫道行於陽而具
於陰也有定名偏於仁而偏於知也無全見此
道之所以鮮能也歟抑考此章首言一陰一陽
之謂道終則曰陰陽不測之謂神于以見天地
punctuated: 道具於陰而行乎陽，以其方出而未賦於物，則繼之者謂之善焉。繼言其發，而善則化育之功。觀夫往過來續，流動充滿於槖籥之間；舊禪新繹，絪緼交密於亭毒之表。純而不雜，善而無惡，是即萬物統體是道之時，陽之事也。及其已出而賦於物，則成之者謂之性焉。成言其具，而性則物之所受。觀夫保合太和，而全其混融之氣；各正性命，而固其陰陽之理。不相假借，不相凌奪，是即萬物各具是道之時，陰之事也。然道之全體本無不具，而人之氣禀或不能齊。是以仁者之人，禀陽氣之多，但見是道流動而無窮，充滿而無間，遂目道之全體止於仁，而不知仁之外復有知焉；知者之人，禀陰氣之多，惟見是道貞靜而不擾，收斂而不露，竟謂道之全體止於知，而不知知之外復有仁焉。噫！道行於陽而具於陰也，有定名；偏於仁而偏於知也，無全見。此道之所以鮮能也歟！抑考此章，首言「一陰一陽之謂道」，終則曰「陰陽不測之謂神」，于以見天地
translation_en:
… the Way is complete in yin and operates through yang. Insofar as it has just emerged and has not yet been endowed upon things, "that which succeeds it is called goodness." "Succeeding" refers to its issuance, while "goodness" is the achievement of transforming and nourishing. Observe how the past departs and the future continues, flowing and filling the space within the cosmic bellows; the old yields and the new unfolds, densely intermingling beyond the shaping and maturing of things. Pure and unadulterated, good and without evil—this is the moment when the myriad things collectively embody this Way, which is the work of yang. When it has already emerged and been endowed upon things, "that which completes it is called nature." "Completing" refers to its being fully present, while "nature" is what things receive. Observe how they preserve and unite in Great Harmony, keeping whole their blended vital energy, and how each rectifies its nature and destiny, making firm its principle of yin and yang. Neither borrowing from one another nor encroaching upon one another—this is the moment when each of the myriad things individually possesses this Way, which is the work of yin.

Yet while the whole substance of the Way is originally lacking in nothing, the endowments of vital energy in human beings cannot always be uniform. Therefore, humane persons, being endowed with an abundance of yang energy, see only that this Way flows without exhaustion and fills everything without gap; thus they regard the whole substance of the Way as stopping at humanity, not knowing that beyond humanity there is also wisdom. Wise persons, being endowed with an abundance of yin energy, see only that this Way is firm, tranquil, and unperturbed, gathered in and unexposed; thus they conclude that the whole substance of the Way stops at wisdom, not knowing that beyond wisdom there is also humanity. Alas! As the Way operates through yang and is complete in yin, it has definite designations; as people lean toward humanity or lean toward wisdom, they lack a complete view. Is this not why few are able to practice the Way? Moreover, if we examine this chapter, it begins by saying, "One yin and one yang are called the Way," and ends by saying, "What is unfathomable in yin and yang is called spirit." From this we may see that between heaven and earth …

text:
間不過陰陽兩端而道行乎其間體謂道而用
謂神也其體其用固不外乎陰陽而其所以然
者則未嘗倚於陰陽也旨哉
變而通之以盡利鼓之舞之以盡神
王崇

妙也盖利者事之宜神者事之妙自非聖人用
易而變通鼓舞之豈能盡利而盡神哉今夫天

以盡其利焉是故化而裁之九六迭用之無常
推而行之剛柔相推之不滯如因也之變而通
之于以盡建侯之利因需之變而通之于以盡

間不過陰陽兩端，而道行乎其間，體謂道而用謂神也。其體其用固不外乎陰陽，而其所以然者，則未嘗倚於陰陽也。旨哉！

變而通之以盡利，鼓之舞之以盡神。

聖人推《易》而見於事，盡乎事之宜而極其用之妙也。盖利者事之宜，神者事之妙。自非聖人用《易》而變通鼓舞之，豈能盡利而盡神哉？今夫天下之事不一，而利無窮。聖人於是用《易》變通之，以盡其利焉。是故化而裁之，九、六迭用之無常；推而行之，剛、柔相推之不滯。如因也之變而通之，于以盡建侯之利；因《需》之變而通之，于以盡涉川之利。《豫》之變也，通之而利用行師；《益》之變也，通之而利有攸往。使天下之事，思慮若或啓…

…between [heaven and earth] there is nothing more than the two polarities of yin and yang, and the Way operates between them: its substance is called the Way and its function is called the numinous. Its substance and its function certainly do not lie outside of yin and yang, yet that by which they are so has never depended upon yin and yang. How profound in meaning!

Wang Chong 王崇

Examiner, Instructor Dai, comments: [The argument is well-ordered and lucid, beyond the reach of superficial compositions.]
Examiner, Instructor Tang, comments: [The composition and reasoning are fluent and clear; it is truly fitting to display it prominently.]

When the sages extended the Book of Changes (Yi) and manifested it in human affairs, they exhausted what was appropriate in affairs and reached the utmost subtlety in its application. For "advantage" is the appropriateness of affairs, and "the numinous" is the subtlety of affairs. Were it not for the sages applying the Changes to adapt and inspire them, how could one exhaust what is advantageous and exhaust the numinous? Now the affairs of the world are not uniform, and their advantages are inexhaustible. The sages therefore used the Changes to change and adapt them in order to exhaust their advantages. Thus, transforming and regulating them, the lines of nine and six are used alternately without fixed regularity; extending and putting them into practice, the firm and the yielding push each other forward without stagnation. For instance, by following the changes of Zhun [transcribed as 也 [?]] and adapting them, they exhausted the advantage of establishing feudal lords; by following the changes of Xu (Waiting) and adapting them, they exhausted the advantage of crossing the great stream. In the changes of Yu (Enthusiasm), they adapted them so that it is advantageous for mobilizing armies; in the changes of Yi (Increase), they adapted them so that it is advantageous to have somewhere to go. Thus in all the affairs of the world, in deliberation it is as if something enlightens…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
之無所施而不宜行焉若或翼之無所往而不
順尚何利之不盡乎利既盡於變通矣然民生
之事萬殊而用至神聖人於是用易鼓舞之以
盡其神焉是故振揚發明而定天下之吉凶提
撕警覺而成天下之亹亹如乾初九當潛也則
鼓之以勿用九二當見也則鼓之以利見鼓舞
觀之用賓于王自然使之興起而無疑鼓舞升
之用見大人自然俾之奮發而不倦使民生日
用趨赴而不知夫誰之功茫乎天運之難名蹻
===
躍而莫測其用之妙杳乎神化之無迹又何神
之不盡乎是知利盡於變通之中而神盡於鼓
舞之內聖人用易之道大矣哉抑此言聖人推
易之道見於事也上文曰聖人立象以盡意設
卦以盡情僞繫辭焉以盡其言聖人發其精意
見於書也見於書者固聖人作易之極功見於
事者尤聖人用易之至神易也神也聖人也何
間然之有
書
punctuated:
之，無所施而不宜；行焉若或翼之，無所往而不順，尚何利之不盡乎？利既盡於變通矣，然民生之事萬殊，而用至神，聖人於是用《易》鼓舞之，以盡其神焉。是故振揚發明，而定天下之吉凶；提撕警覺，而成天下之亹亹。如《乾》初九當潛也，則鼓之以「勿用」；九二當見也，則鼓之以「利見」。鼓舞《觀》之「用賓于王」，自然使之興起而無疑；鼓舞《升》之「用見大人」，自然俾之奮發而不倦。使民生日用趨赴，而不知夫誰之功，茫乎天運之難名；蹻躍而莫測其用之妙，杳乎神化之無迹，又何神之不盡乎？是知利盡於變通之中，而神盡於鼓舞之內，聖人用《易》之道大矣哉！抑此言聖人推《易》之道見於事也。上文曰：「聖人立象以盡意，設卦以盡情僞，繫辭焉以盡其言。」聖人發其精意，見於書也。見於書者，固聖人作《易》之極功；見於事者，尤聖人用《易》之至神。《易》也，神也，聖人也，何間然之有！
《書》
translation_en:
… them, so that there is nothing they apply to that is not fitting; in action it is as if something gives them wings, so that there is nowhere they go that does not prosper—then what benefit is not exhausted? Once benefit is exhausted through change and adaptation, yet the affairs of the people's lives are myriad in their variety and their functioning is supremely marvelous, the sages thereupon use the Book of Changes (Yi) to inspire and rouse them as if by drum and dance, so as to exhaust its marvelousness. Therefore, by rousing and illuminating, they determine the good and bad fortune of all under heaven; by awakening and alerting, they bring to completion the tireless endeavors of all under heaven. For example, when the first nine line of the Qian hexagram ought to remain hidden, they rouse them with "Do not act"; when the second nine line ought to appear, they rouse them with "It is advantageous to see." By inspiring and rousing with the Guan hexagram's "It is advantageous to be the guest of the king," they naturally cause people to rise up without doubt; by inspiring and rousing with the Sheng hexagram's "It is advantageous to see the great man," they naturally cause people to exert themselves without tiring. They cause the people in their daily lives to hasten forward without knowing whose achievement it is—vast and boundless like the operation of Heaven that is hard to name; leaping into action without fathoming the subtlety of its functioning—profound and indistinct like divine transformation that leaves no trace. Then what marvelousness is not exhausted? From this we know that benefit is exhausted within change and adaptation, and marvelousness is exhausted within inspiring and rousing. Great indeed is the Way by which the sages use the Changes! Moreover, this speaks of the sages extending the Way of the Changes as manifested in affairs. The preceding text says: "The sages set up images to exhaust their ideas, established hexagrams to exhaust the genuine and the false, and appended judgments to exhaust their words." That is the sages expressing their subtle ideas as manifested in writing. What is manifested in writing is indeed the ultimate achievement of the sages in making the Changes; what is manifested in affairs is especially the supreme marvelousness of the sages in using the Changes. The Changes, the marvelous, and the sages—what gap is there among them!

皐陶曰俞師汝昌言禹曰都帝慎乃在位
曰思明

大臣然同列之言而欲法於已同列致歎美之
辭而必戒於君盖虞廷君臣之心儆戒無虞之
心也大禹因皐陶深契保治之言安得不致歎
===
美而歸戒於其君哉且大禹之陳謨正皐陶之
在側心孚意契而深然之言不覺形諸聲志同
道合而深信之念自然發於外盖謂洪水滔天
而隨山濬川卒致萬邦作乂之休此汝之昌言
也是言也警戒之意實寓於其間豈非盛德之
言在我今日所當師法者乎下民昏墊而暨益
暨稷同底烝民乃粒之效亦汝之昌言也是言
也保治之意實存於其中又非盛德之言在我
今日所當取法者乎大禹一聞斯言即契於中
punctuated:
「皐陶曰：『俞，師汝昌言。』禹曰：『都！帝慎乃在位。』」
曰思明
同考試官訓導鄒　批：〔場中作此題者，多不知昌言寓儆戒之意，此篇文理切當，宜冠本房。〕

大臣然同列之言而欲法於已，同列致歎美之辭而必戒於君。盖虞廷君臣之心，儆戒無虞之心也。大禹因皐陶深契保治之言，安得不致歎美而歸戒於其君哉？且大禹之陳謨，正皐陶之在側。心孚意契，而深然之言不覺形諸聲；志同道合，而深信之念自然發於外。盖謂洪水滔天，而隨山濬川，卒致萬邦作乂之休，此汝之昌言也。是言也，警戒之意實寓於其間，豈非盛德之言，在我今日所當師法者乎？下民昏墊，而暨益暨稷，同底烝民乃粒之效，亦汝之昌言也。是言也，保治之意實存於其中，又非盛德之言，在我今日所當取法者乎？大禹一聞斯言，即契於中，

"Gao Yao said, 'Indeed! I take your splendid words as my model.' Yu said, 'Oh! Emperor, be cautious on your throne.'"

Yue Siming 曰思明

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Zou 鄒, commented: [Among those in the examination hall writing on this topic, most failed to realize that the "splendid words" [rendered here as 習言] carry the meaning of admonition and caution. The literary reasoning of this essay is apt and fitting; it ought to top this ward.]
Examiner, Instructor Dai 戴, commented: [It elucidates the purport of admonition and caution, leaving almost no subtle meaning unexpressed.]
Examiner, Instructor Tang 唐, commented: [It capably elucidates the intent of Yu and Gao Yao in mutually counseling one another to serve their sovereign; it is commendable.]

When a great minister approves the words of his colleague and wishes to take them as a model for himself, that colleague utters expressions of admiration and praise yet invariably directs an admonition to his sovereign. For the mind of the sovereign and ministers at the court of Yu 虞 [Shun] was a mind of admonition and caution even when there was nothing to fear. Because Great Yu found that Gao Yao deeply resonated with his words on preserving good governance, how could he not express admiration and direct his admonition back to his sovereign?

Moreover, when Great Yu set forth his counsels, Gao Yao was right by his side. With their minds in accord and their intentions aligned, words of deep approval unconsciously took form in his voice; sharing the same aspirations and walking the same Way, thoughts of deep conviction naturally issued forth on the outside. He meant to say: "When the floodwaters swelled to heaven, going along the mountains and deepening the rivers, thereby ultimately achieving the blessing of all the myriad states being brought to order—these were your splendid words. Within these words, the intent of vigilance and caution truly resides; are they not words of flourishing virtue that I ought to take as a model today? Within these words, the intent of preserving good governance truly exists; are they not also words of flourishing virtue that I ought to emulate today?" title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
故都以歎其美稱帝以起其聽意謂烝民乃粒
世固可謂無虞矣然天位惟艱一念不謹或以
貽四海之憂要必惟精惟一兢兢以存此心於
四方風動之時可也萬邦作乂世固可謂無事
矣然厭位惟危一日不謹或以致千百年之患
要必惟幾惟康業業以致其治於庶績咸熙之
日可也虞廷大臣規戒其君如此其忠愛之心
爲何如哉嗟夫舜嘗使禹亦如皐陶昌言矣故
禹因孜孜之義而述其治水本末先後之詳蓋
===
欲君臣上下相與保治於無窮皐陶從而俞之
而以其言爲可法禹又都之而推其意戒於君
所謂以道事君者此所以庶雍熙泰和之盛
卒乎不可尚也歟
終始慎厥與惟明明后先王惟時懋敬厥
德克配上帝今王嗣有令緒尚監茲哉
皇明
同考試官訓導鄒 批發明伊尹欲太甲圖終而
與成湯之治同道勝有理緻可嘉
punctuated:
故都以歎其美，稱帝以起其聽。意謂烝民乃粒，世固可謂無虞矣。然天位惟艱，一念不謹，或以貽四海之憂，要必惟精惟一，兢兢以存此心於四方風動之時可也。萬邦作乂，世固可謂無事矣。然厭位惟危，一日不謹，或以致千百年之患，要必惟幾惟康，業業以致其治於庶績咸熙之日可也。虞廷大臣規戒其君如此，其忠愛之心爲何如哉！嗟夫，舜嘗使禹亦如皐陶昌言矣，故禹因孜孜之義，而述其治水本末先後之詳，蓋欲君臣上下相與保治於無窮。皐陶從而俞之，而以其言爲可法；禹又都之，而推其意戒於君。所謂以道事君者此，所以庶雍熙泰和之盛，卒乎不可尚也歟！

「終始慎厥與，惟明明后。先王惟時懋敬厥德，克配上帝。今王嗣有令緒，尚監茲哉！」
皇明
同考試官訓導鄒批：發明伊尹欲太甲圖終，而與成湯之治同道，勝有理緻，可嘉。
translation_en:
…Therefore he exclaimed "Oh!" to praise its excellence, and addressed the Emperor to arouse his attention. His meaning was that since the multitude of the people now had grain to eat, the world could indeed be called free from anxiety. Yet the Heavenly seat is difficult; if a single thought is not cautious, it might bequeath sorrow to the Four Seas. Essentially, one must be discriminating and undivided, cautiously preserving this mind at a time when the four quarters are moved as by the wind—only then will it do. Since the myriad states were brought to order, the world could indeed be called free from trouble. Yet the throne [reading 厥 for 厭][?] is perilous; if for a single day one is not cautious, it might bring about calamity for hundreds or thousands of years. Essentially, one must attend to the subtle springs of things and to repose, fearfully andisiuously achieving good governance in the days when all achievements are resplendent—only then will it do. The great ministers of the court of Yu admonished their ruler in this manner; how great were their hearts of loyalty and affection! Alas, Shun had once bade Yu also to speak flourishing words like Gao Yao. Therefore Yu, building upon the meaning of unwearying diligence, recounted in detail the beginning and end, the sequence of his controlling the waters, desiring that ruler and ministers, high and low, should together preserve good governance without end. Gao Yao thereupon said "Yes!" to it, taking his words as worthy to be made a model; Yu in turn exclaimed "Oh!" and extended their meaning to admonish the ruler. This is what is meant by serving the ruler according to the Way; is this not why the flourishing of universal harmony and great peace in Yu [reading 虞 for 庶][?] proved ultimately unsurpassable?

"From beginning to end be cautious about whom you associate with; thus will you be a brightly intelligent sovereign. The former king was always earnestly reverent of his virtue, and so was able to be a counterpart to Shangdi. Now Your Majesty has succeeded to the fine inheritance; may you take this as your mirror!"

Imperial Ming [candidate].
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zou comments: It elucidates how Yi Yin desired Tai Jia to plan for the end and share the same Way as the governance of Cheng Tang. It is superior in its close-knit reasoning and worthy of praise.

大臣告君以謹與治之心而愈極其明正欲其
與前聖之治而必同其道夫古人之治後人所
當與者也大臣欲賢王謹其所與而為至明之
君安得不舉前聖之治而勉其同道也哉在昔
伊尹申誥太甲謂夫始焉與治固可以興終焉
或替則非所以為明君矣要必謹其所與終始
惟一不以悠久而貳其心焉是惟明而又明之
===
君為能然而懋昭大德灼于四方矣前日與治
固可以興後日不繼亦非所以為明后矣要必
慎其所與前後惟一不以有永而易其念焉是
惟明而又明之后為能然而丕顯惟德光于天
下矣今王於此而欲與治同道舍成湯何以哉
是故勇智天錫其德固不待於懋懋敬矣惟湯也
兢兢焉昧爽丕顯而與上天生物之仁同一機

大臣告君以謹與治之心，而愈極其明，正欲其與前聖之治而必同其道。夫古人之治，後人所當與者也。大臣欲賢王謹其所與而為至明之君，安得不舉前聖之治而勉其同道也哉？在昔伊尹申誥太甲，謂夫始焉與治，固可以興；終焉或替，則非所以為明君矣。要必謹其所與，終始惟一，不以悠久而貳其心焉，是惟明而又明之君為能然，而懋昭大德，灼于四方矣。前日與治，固可以興；後日不繼，亦非所以為明后矣。要必慎其所與，前後惟一，不以有永而易其念焉，是惟明而又明之后為能然，而丕顯惟德，光于天下矣。今王於此而欲與治同道，舍成湯何以哉？是故勇智天錫，其德固不待於懋懋敬矣，惟湯也，兢兢焉昧爽丕顯，而與上天生物之仁同一機；聖敬日躋，其德亦不俟於懋敬矣，惟湯也，業業焉顧諟明命，而與上天不已之誠同一致。德與…

When the great minister counsels his ruler to be cautious in his commitment to aligning with well-ordered governance, thereby bringing his illumination to the utmost perfection, it is precisely because he wishes him to share without fail the same Way as the governance of the former sage. Now, the governance of the ancients is what later generations ought to align themselves with. When the great minister wished the worthy king to be cautious in what he aligned himself with and to become a supremely enlightened ruler, how could he not hold up the governance of the former sage and urge him to share that same Way? In antiquity, when Yi Yin 伊尹 repeated his announcements to Tai Jia 太甲, he meant that if at the beginning one aligns with well-ordered governance, one can certainly rise to prosperity; yet if in the end one allows it to lapse, that is not the way to be an enlightened ruler. Above all, one must be cautious in what one aligns with, remaining single-minded from beginning to end and never letting one's heart waver because of the long passage of time. Only a ruler who is enlightened and ever more enlightened is capable of this, thereby vigorously manifesting his great virtue so that it shines forth throughout the four quarters. If on a former day one aligns with well-ordered governance, one can certainly rise to prosperity; yet if on a later day one fails to sustain it, that too is not the way to be an enlightened sovereign. Above all, one must be careful in what one aligns with, remaining single-minded before and after and never altering one's resolve over a prolonged duration. Only a sovereign who is enlightened and ever more enlightened is capable of this, thereby grandly displaying his virtue so that it illuminates all under heaven. title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
天合心與天契故克配上帝而無間矣今王繼
成湯之丕基承成湯之令緒其可不以成湯為
監而與治同其道乎伊尹以是為太甲告忠愛
之心何其至哉考之太甲蓋嘗弗明于德矣一
旦悔過而曰尚賴匡救之德圖惟厥終故伊尹
復進圖終之說而欲其與湯之治同道如此厥
後太甲克終允德為商令王謂非伊尹告戒之
功而誰歟
爾惟弘周公丕訓無依勢作威無倚法以
削寛而有制從容以和敞民在辟予曰辟
爾惟勿辟予曰宥爾惟勿宥惟厥中
董通
同考試官訓導鄒　批〔此作以傳註組織成文說〕
出成王慮君陳狥己狥君之意甚明
考試官教諭戴　批〔文理暢達初考得之〕

賢君命大臣不惟慮其狥己而戒勉之辭切尤
必慮其狥君而責望之意深夫大臣位君民之
punctuated:
天合，心與天契，故克配上帝而無間矣。今王繼成湯之丕基，承成湯之令緒，其可不以成湯為監，而與治同其道乎？伊尹以是為太甲告，忠愛之心何其至哉！考之太甲，蓋嘗弗明于德矣。一旦悔過，而曰：「尚賴匡救之德，圖惟厥終。」故伊尹復進圖終之說，而欲其與湯之治同道如此。厥後太甲克終允德，為商令王，謂非伊尹告戒之功而誰歟？

爾惟弘周公丕訓，無依勢作威，無倚法以削。寛而有制，從容以和。敞民在辟，予曰辟，爾惟勿辟；予曰宥，爾惟勿宥，惟厥中。

賢君命大臣，不惟慮其狥己而戒勉之辭切，尤必慮其狥君而責望之意深。夫大臣位君民之
translation_en:
… united with Heaven and his mind was in accord with Heaven; therefore he was able to be a counterpart to the Lord on High without the slightest gap. Now Your Majesty succeeds to Tang the Successful's great foundation and inherits Tang the Successful's fine patrimony—how could you not take Tang the Successful as a mirror and share the same Way as his governance? Yi Yin 伊尹 spoke thus to Tai Jia 太甲; how utmost was his loyal and loving heart! Examining the case of Tai Jia, he had once been unenlightened in virtue. Once he repented of his faults and said, "I still rely on your corrective and saving virtue, seeking to plan for the end," Yi Yin therefore again presented this explanation of planning for the end, wishing him to share the same Way as Tang's governance in this manner. Thereafter Tai Jia was able to bring his sincere virtue to completion and became a fine king of Shang—if one were to say this was not the achievement of Yi Yin's admonitions, whose was it?

"You must enlarge upon the great instructions of the Duke of Zhou: do not rely on power to exercise severity, and do not lean on the law to pare down the people. Be寬 indulgent yet have regulation, and be unhurried so as to achieve harmony. When the殷 [here written 敞, *chang*] people are subject to punishment, if I say 'punish,' do not punish; if I say 'pardon,' do not pardon—seek only the due mean."

Dong Tong 董通.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zou 鄒 comments: 〔This composition weaves the commentary notes into an essay, explaining〕 very clearly King Cheng's 成王 concern that Jun Chen 君陳 might indulge himself or defer to his ruler.
Examiner and Instructor Dai 戴 comments: 〔The reasoning and style are fluent and lucid; it was selected in the initial reading.〕
Examiner and Instructor Tang 唐 comments: 〔The principles are clear and the language concise; it grasps the purport of King Cheng's charge to Jun Chen.〕

When a worthy ruler gives a charge to a great minister, not only is he concerned lest the minister indulge himself, making his words of admonition and encouragement earnest, he is even more concerned lest the minister defer blindly to the ruler, making the intent of his expectations deep. Now, a great minister occupies a position between the ruler and the people…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
兩間固當行其事之所當行也然則化民其可
徇乎已用刑其可徇乎君哉此成王之命君陳
所以戒勉於前而責望於後也且其意若曰東
郊之民周公蓋嘗師保矣今爾往茲以繼其治
要必弘大公之丕訓常在人心而不忘焉下都
之民周公亦嘗謹毖矣今爾尹茲以代其政要
必開拓公之大訓恒在民心而不泯焉然勢我
所有也不可依之以至於作威法我所用也不
可倚之而至於以削況君陳之世當寬和之時
===
也寬不可一於寬必寬而有其制可也和不可
一於和必從容以和之可也夫化民而徇已固
爾之所當戒用刑而徇君又孰非爾之所當謹
乎是故殷民之在刑辟我雖以為是固可辟也
爾毋徇我之情而辟之惟當審其輕重之中而
辟其所當辟焉商民之罹刑罰我雖以為是固
可宥也爾毋徇我之意而宥之惟當審其輕重
之中而宥其所當宥焉賢王以是為大臣告其
圖治之心一何至哉按此篇言周公之訓屢矣
punctuated: 兩間，固當行其事之所當行也。然則化民其可徇乎已？用刑其可徇乎君哉？此成王之命君陳，所以戒勉於前而責望於後也。且其意若曰：東郊之民，周公蓋嘗師保矣；今爾往茲，以繼其治，要必弘大公之丕訓，常在人心而不忘焉。下都之民，周公亦嘗謹毖矣；今爾尹茲，以代其政，要必開拓公之大訓，恒在民心而不泯焉。然勢，我所有也，不可依之以至於作威；法，我所用也，不可倚之而至於以削。況君陳之世，當寬和之時也。寬不可一於寬，必寬而有其制可也；和不可一於和，必從容以和之可也。夫化民而徇已，固爾之所當戒；用刑而徇君，又孰非爾之所當謹乎？是故殷民之在刑辟，我雖以為是固可辟也，爾毋徇我之情而辟之，惟當審其輕重之中而辟其所當辟焉。商民之罹刑罰，我雖以為是固可宥也，爾毋徇我之意而宥之，惟當審其輕重之中而宥其所當宥焉。賢王以是為大臣告，其圖治之心一何至哉！按此篇言周公之訓屢矣，
translation_en:
…between the two, he should naturally carry out the duties that ought to be carried out. How then, in transforming the people, could he indulge himself? And in applying punishments, how could he merely comply with the ruler? This is why King Cheng, in giving his charge to Junchen, first admonished and encouraged him, and subsequently placed such expectations and responsibilities upon him.

Moreover, his meaning was as if to say: "As for the people of the eastern suburbs, the Duke of Zhou once acted as their teacher and protector; now that you go there to continue his governance, you must amplify and enlarge the Duke's great instructions, so that they always remain in the people's hearts and are not forgotten. As for the people of the lower capital, the Duke of Zhou also once cautiously admonished them; now that you govern there to take over his administration, you must expand and develop the Duke's great instructions, so that they constantly remain in the people's minds and do not perish. Yet power is what you possess; you must not rely upon it to the point of playing the tyrant. Law is what you employ; you must not lean upon it to the point of cruel exaction. How much more so since the era of Junchen falls at a time calling for leniency and harmony! Leniency must not be mere one-sided leniency; there must be leniency accompanied by proper regulation. Harmony must not be mere one-sided harmony; one must harmonize them with unhurried composure. Now, indulging yourself in transforming the people is certainly what you must guard against; and in applying punishments, is not complying with the ruler also something about which you must be cautious? Therefore, when the people of Yin fall under criminal punishment, even though I may deem that they certainly ought to be punished, do not comply with my feelings and punish them, but only examine the due mean between light and heavy, and punish those who ought to be punished. When the people of Shang incur penal sanctions, even though I may deem that they certainly ought to be pardoned, do not comply with my wishes and pardon them, but only examine the due mean between light and heavy, and pardon those who ought to be pardoned."

When a worthy king thus instructs his great ministers, how utmost is his heart in planning for good governance! Now, looking at this chapter, it speaks repeatedly of the instructions of the Duke of Zhou:…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
曰懋昭曰式時至是又欲君陳弘公丕訓何歟
蓋周公既没民方思慕周公之訓君陳能盡張
而大之其不翕然而聽順乎故成王以弘公丕
訓為言而特戒其徇己徇君之失可謂知所本
矣然則君陳可不思所以副其望哉
詩
南有樛木葛藟纍之樂只君子福履綏之
南有樛木葛藟荒之樂只君子福履將之
南有樛木葛藟縈之樂只君子福履成之
趙愽
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔此題頭緒頗多作者泛而不切是篇簡明宜冠本房〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔詞約理備允宜録出〕
考試官教諭唐　批〔善於鋪叙理亦詳明〕
===
詩人屢即地勢生物而為微物所附以興女德
逮下而為盛福所歸蓋德者福之本也今后妃
有逮下之德豈不為福禄之所歸哉宜詩人屢
托興而義之也昔后妃能逮下而無嫉妬之心
punctuated:
曰「懋昭」、曰「式時」，至是又欲君陳弘公丕訓，何歟？蓋周公既没，民方思慕周公之訓，君陳能盡張而大之，其不翕然而聽順乎？故成王以弘公丕訓為言，而特戒其徇己、徇君之失，可謂知所本矣。然則君陳可不思所以副其望哉？

詩
「南有樛木，葛藟纍之。樂只君子，福履綏之。南有樛木，葛藟荒之。樂只君子，福履將之。南有樛木，葛藟縈之。樂只君子，福履成之。」
趙愽
同考試官教諭蔣批：〔此題頭緒頗多，作者泛而不切，是篇簡明，宜冠本房。〕
考試官教諭戴批：〔詞約理備，允宜録出。〕
考試官教諭唐批：〔善於鋪叙，理亦詳明。〕

詩人屢即地勢生物而為微物所附，以興女德逮下而為盛福所歸。蓋德者，福之本也。今后妃有逮下之德，豈不為福禄之所歸哉？宜詩人屢托興而義之也。昔后妃能逮下而無嫉妬之心，
translation_en:
… saying “strive to make illustrious,” saying “take as a model”; and coming to this point he again wishes Jun Chen (君陳) to enlarge the Duke’s great teachings—why is this? Indeed, after the Duke of Zhou (周公) had died, the people were just then longing with affection for the teachings of the Duke of Zhou. If Jun Chen could fully extend and magnify them, would they not harmoniously listen and obey? Therefore King Cheng (成王) spoke in terms of enlarging the Duke’s great teachings, while specifically warning him against the faults of indulging himself or indulging his ruler; he may well be said to have known what was fundamental. This being so, how could Jun Chen not ponder how to live up to his expectations?

Classic of Poetry (Shijing 詩經)
“In the south there are trees with drooping branches, the kudzu and wild grape vines bind them. / Oh, happy is our lord [lady]! May blessings and dignity comfort her! / In the south there are trees with drooping branches, the kudzu and wild grape vines cover them. / Oh, happy is our lady! May blessings and dignity sustain her! / In the south there are trees with drooping branches, the kudzu and wild grape vines entwine them. / Oh, happy is our lady! May blessings and dignity bring her fulfillment!”
By Zhao Bo (趙愽)
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Jiang (蔣): [This topic has rather many threads; most writers were vague and missed the mark, whereas this essay is concise and clear, and deserves to head this examination ward.]
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Dai (戴): [Its wording is concise and its reasoning complete; it truly deserves to be selected for publication.]
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Tang (唐): [Skillful in exposition, and its reasoning is also detailed and clear.]

The poet repeatedly takes up how the terrain produces living things to which humble plants attach themselves, so as to evoke how feminine virtue reaches down to inferiors and becomes that to which abundant blessings return. For virtue is the root of blessing. Now, since the queen consort possesses the virtue of reaching down to her inferiors, how could she not become the one to whom blessings and emoluments return? Truly it is fitting that the poet repeatedly relies on evocative imagery to set forth the meaning of this [?]. In former times, the queen consort was able to extend her grace down to her inferiors without a jealous heart, …

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
故衆妾樂其德而稱願之曰彼南山之地木之
所生而有下曲之狀是以葛藟得以纍而繫之
也匪特繫之而已尤必荒而奄之不殊乎蔦與
女蘿施于松柏矣匪但荒之而已尤且縈而旋
之不殊乎蔦與女蘿施于松上矣木之所生尚
為微物之所附況樂只君子有不為福祿之所
歸耶然后妃之德慈惠貞靜而有可樂之實是
以福祿有以綏而安之也不特安之而已尤必
將而扶助之奚翅俾爾多益以莫不庶焉不但
===
將之而已尤且以而成就之奚翅降爾遐福維
日不足焉噫上無而下附此感而彼孚自有不
期然而然矣詩人以是形諸詠歌其亦深知后
妃之德者歟嘗考后妃之德關雎舉其全體而
言也葛覃卷耳言其志行之在己樛木螽斯美
其德惠之及人皆指一事而言也其詞雖主於
后妃然其實則皆所以著明文王身脩家齊之
效也讀詩者不可不知
汎汎楊舟載沉載浮既見君子我心則休
punctuated:
故衆妾樂其德而稱願之曰：彼南山之地，木之所生而有下曲之狀，是以葛藟得以纍而繫之也。匪特繫之而已，尤必荒而奄之，不殊乎「蔦與女蘿，施于松柏」矣；匪但荒之而已，尤且縈而旋之，不殊乎「蔦與女蘿，施于松上」矣。木之所生，尚為微物之所附，況樂只君子，有不為福祿之所歸耶？然后妃之德，慈惠貞靜，而有可樂之實，是以福祿有以綏而安之也。不特安之而已，尤必將而扶助之，奚翅「俾爾多益，以莫不庶」焉；不但將之而已，尤且以而成就之，奚翅「降爾遐福，維日不足」焉。噫！上無而下附，此感而彼孚，自有不期然而然矣。詩人以是形諸詠歌，其亦深知后妃之德者歟！嘗考后妃之德，《關雎》舉其全體而言也，《葛覃》、《卷耳》言其志行之在己，《樛木》、《螽斯》美其德惠之及人，皆指一事而言也。其詞雖主於后妃，然其實則皆所以著明文王身脩家齊之效也，讀《詩》者不可不知。
汎汎楊舟，載沉載浮。既見君子，我心則休。
translation_en:
…Therefore, the various concubines delighted in her virtue and praised and wished her well, saying: That land of the Southern Mountain, where trees grow and have downward-curving branches, is why the kudzu and wild grape vines are able to entwine and bind themselves to them. Not only do they bind themselves to them, they even cover and overspread them, no different from how "the mistletoe and the dodder spread over the pine and the cypress." Not only do they cover them, they moreover wind and coil around them, no different from how "the mistletoe and the dodder spread atop the pine." If even the trees that grow there are clung to by humble plants, how much more so this joyous noble lady—how could she not be the one to whom blessings and emoluments return? Now, the virtue of the Queen Consort is benevolent, kind, chaste, and tranquil, possessing the true substance that inspires joy; therefore, blessings and emoluments comfort and give her peace. Not only do they give her peace, they certainly support and assist her—how is this any less than "making you richly endowed, so that there is nothing not abundant"? Not only do they support her, they moreover bring her to fulfillment [?]—how is this any less than "sending down upon you far-reaching blessings, for which the days are not long enough"? Alas! When the superior shelters [?] and the inferior clings, when this side moves and that side trusts in response, it naturally comes about without being sought. The poet gave form to this in song; was he not also one who deeply understood the virtue of the Queen Consort? If we examine the virtue of the Queen Consort, "Guanju" (The Osprey's Cry) speaks of it in its entirety; "Getan" (The Spreading Kudzu) and "Juan'er" (The Cocklebur) speak of the aspirations and conduct within herself; "Jiumu" (The Drooping Trees) and "Zhongsi" (The Locusts) praise her virtuous kindness reaching others—each pointing to a single aspect. Although the words focus on the Queen Consort, in reality they all serve to make manifest the efficacy of King Wen's cultivating his person and regulating his family. Readers of the Odes (Shi) must not fail to know this.

Floating, floating is the poplar boat, now sinking, now bobbing. Having seen the lord, my heart is then at rest.

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
趙傅
同考試官教諭蔣　批此題作者往往認為
興體殊失本旨是篇文理通暢可取
考試官教諭戴　批能發明未見既見之意可嘉
考試官教諭唐　批辭理俱到宜在高選
詩人既喻人君未見賢者而心為不定必言人
君已見賢者而心為始安夫賢者人君素所願
見也未見之時其心固不能定矣既見之後其
心容有不安者哉思昔人君燕飲賓客而追言
===
好賢之心謂夫以汎汎楊舟而在彼中流載沉
載浮未定也然其所以沉浮而未定者正猶人
君未見君子憂心為之怲怲也以汎汎楊舟而
在彼中河載沉載浮未安也然其所以沉浮而
未安者正如人君未覯君子憂心為之忡忡也
夫向而未見其心固不能安矣今而亦既見止
則有以洽夫笑語之樂而思慕之懷于焉而寫
矣其心豈不休休然而安定乎昔而未覯其心
固不能定矣今而亦既覯止則有以關其大道
punctuated:
趙傅。
同考試官教諭蔣批：「此題作者往往認為興體，殊失本旨。是篇文理通暢，可取。」
考試官教諭戴批：「能發明未見、既見之意，可嘉。」
考試官教諭唐批：「辭理俱到，宜在高選。」
詩人既喻人君未見賢者而心為不定，必言人君已見賢者而心為始安。夫賢者，人君素所願見也。未見之時，其心固不能定矣；既見之後，其心容有不安者哉？思昔人君燕飲賓客，而追言好賢之心，謂夫以汎汎楊舟而在彼中流，載沉載浮，未定也。然其所以沉浮而未定者，正猶人君未見君子，憂心為之怲怲也。以汎汎楊舟而在彼中河，載沉載浮，未安也。然其所以沉浮而未安者，正如人君未覯君子，憂心為之忡忡也。夫向而未見，其心固不能安矣；今而亦既見止，則有以洽夫笑語之樂，而思慕之懷于焉而寫矣，其心豈不休休然而安定乎？昔而未覯，其心固不能定矣；今而亦既覯止，則有以關其大道
translation_en:
Zhao Fu 趙傅.
Associate Examiner Instructor Jiang 蔣 comments: "Writers on this topic often take it to be in the evocative mode (xing 興), which quite misses the original purport [since Zhu Xi takes it as metaphorical, bi 比]. This essay is coherent and fluent in both style and reasoning, and is worthy of selection."
Examiner Instructor Dai 戴 comments: "Able to elucidate the meaning of 'not yet having seen' and 'already having seen'—commendable."
Examiner Instructor Tang 唐 comments: "Both diction and reasoning reach the mark; he ought to be placed high among the selected."
Having used a metaphor for how the ruler's mind is unsettled when he has not yet seen the worthy men, the poet necessarily speaks of how the ruler's mind first becomes at ease once he has seen the worthy men. Now, worthy men are those whom a ruler has always wished to see. When he has not yet seen them, his mind certainly cannot be settled; after he has seen them, how could his mind possibly remain uneasy? Reflecting on how the ruler of old feasted his guests and retrospectively expressed his heart that loved the worthy, the poet says that when a drifting poplar boat is out there in midstream, now sinking, now floating, it is unsettled. Yet its sinking and floating without being settled is just like the ruler who, having not yet seen the noble men, has an anxious heart that is full of distress. When a drifting poplar boat is out there in the middle of the river, now sinking, now floating, it is not at rest. Yet its sinking and floating without being at rest is just like the ruler who, having not yet met the noble men, has an anxious heart that is full of agitation. In the past, when he had not yet seen them, his mind certainly could not be at rest; now that he has indeed seen them, he is able to share harmoniously in the joy of laughter and conversation, and his feelings of longing and admiration are thereby relieved—how could his mind not be happily at peace and settled? Formerly, when he had not yet met them, his mind certainly could not be settled; now that he has indeed met them, he is able to [?] open up [關, perhaps for 開 or 闡?] the great Way…

title: 天順六年山西鄉試錄
text:
之隙而景慕之願于焉而遂矣其心又豈不休
休然而安寧乎詩人即彼喻此可謂善於咏歌
者矣抑考是詩凡四章前二章見人君於賢者
愛敬之心兩盡後二章見人君於賢者樂之如
得重貨之多而又言其未見既見之心也好賢
之意何其深長有若是歟
同考試官教諭蔣　批作者於式南邦作爾庸
李經
王命申伯式是南邦因是謝人以作爾庸
===
處多矣發明此作得之
考試官教諭戴　批作崧高義者僅見此篇
考試官教諭唐　批詩正而葩此作近之
王者命親臣而示法於人因斯民而肇建其國
蓋命親臣而示法於人固王者責望之盛心因
斯民而肇建其國尤王者寵遇之深意宣王之
舅申伯出封于謝而尹吉甫作詩以送之其言
如此謂夫備亹亹之德者申伯也今而宣王封
爾于謝非徒封之也實欲爲法於南國之諸侯
punctuated:
之隙，而景慕之願于焉而遂矣，其心又豈不休休然而安寧乎？詩人即彼喻此，可謂善於咏歌者矣。抑考是詩凡四章：前二章見人君於賢者愛敬之心兩盡，後二章見人君於賢者樂之如得重貨之多，而又言其未見、既見之心也。好賢之意，何其深長有若是歟！

王命申伯，式是南邦；因是謝人，以作爾庸。
李經
